Definition: a tree (from its firmness); hence, wood (plural sticks)
BiblicalUsage: ʻÊts is a tree — and by extension, wood, the stuff trees are made of. The tree of life stood in the garden, the tree of knowledge brought the Fall, and the psalmist's righteous man is like a tree planted by rivers of water. It is the word for rooted, growing, fruitful life.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe ʻêts is the Bible's picture of the blessed life: planted, watered, and bearing fruit in season. I hold that the tree planted by the rivers of water is the end of the story too — rooted, growing, and bearing fruit.
